newsitem.title: LUXEMBOURG: Court applies migrant worker rules to child-raising benefits.
newsitem.headline: Court applies migrant worker rules to child-raising benefits.

text.p: The European Court of Justice ruled on Thursday a child-raising allowance is a family benefit, and the distinction between personal rights and derived rights does not apply.
Spouses of workers entitled under German law to child-raising benefits may receive those benefits whether or not they reside in Germany, the court said.

To decide if a benefit falls under the scope of Community regulation on benefits for migrant workers, courts must decide if the state benefit is granted without "individual and discretionary assessment of personal needs ... and if it concerns one of the risks expressly listed in (the Community regulation)," the court said.
The court said the child raising allowance at issue in this case meets those conditions, and therefore is subject to Community rules for migrant workers.

"If ... the granting of child-raising allowance were subject to the condition that the spouse of a worker, who is not resident in Germany, must be employed within the territory to which the (German law) applies, the worker could be deterred from exercising his right to freedom of movement," the court said.
Germany argued unsuccessfully that the benefit was originally intended for single parent families, and not to benefit spouses residing outside of Germany

The women did not claim to be employed persons but argued they were eligible for derived rights acquired through their husbands' status. The court said the women must personally meet the eligibility requirements for a child-raising allowance under German law, i.e., they could not be employed for more than 15 hours a week.
EXCERPTS FROM THE JUDGMENT
(Court translation into English. Original language of the case: German)
"Social security - Family benefits - Article 73 of regulation (EEC) NO 1408/71 - Article 4(1) of direcive 79/7/EEC - Article 7(2) of regulation (EEC) No 1612/68)
In Joined Cases C-245/94 and C-312/94
Reference by the Landessozialgericht Nordrhein-Westfalen (Germany) for a preliminary ruling in the proceedings pending before that court between
Ingrid Hoever, Iris Zachow
and
Land Nordrhein-Westfalen

on the interpretation of articles 4(1)(h) and 73 of regulation (EEC) No 1408/71 of the Council of 14 June 1971 on the application of social security schemes to employed persons, to self-employed persons and to members of their families moving within the Community (OJ, English Special Edition 1971 (II), p. 416), in the version amended and updated by Council regulation (EEC) No 2001/83 of 2 June 1983 (OJ 1983L 230, p. 6), as amended by Council regulation (EEC) No 3427/89 of 30 October 1989 (OJ 1989 L 331, p. 1), of article 4(1) of Council directive 79/7/EEC of 19 December 1978 on the progressive implementation of the principle of equal treatment for men and women in matters of social security (OJ 1979 L 6, p. 24) and of article 7(2) of regulation (EEC) No 1612/68 of the Council of 15 October 1968 on freedom of movement for workers within the Community (OJ English Special Edition 1968 (II), p. 475)
THE COURT hereby rules

1. A benefit such as the child-raising allowance provided for by the Bundeserziehungsgeldgesetz, which is automatically granted to persons fulfilling certain objective criteria, without any individual and discretionary assessment of personal needs, and which is intended to meet family expenses, must be treated as a family benefit within the meaning of article 4(1)(h) of regulation (EEC) No 1408/71 of the Council of 14 June 1971 on the application of social security schemes to employed persons, to self-employed persons and to members of their families moving within the Community, in the version amended and updated by Council regulation (EEC) No 2001/83, as amended by Council regulation (EEC) NO 3427/89 of 30 October 1989.

2. Where an employed person is subject to the legislation of a member state and lives with his or her family in another member state, that person's spouse is entitled, under article 73 of regulation No 1408/71, to receive a benefit such as child raising allowance in the state of employment.

3. Article 3(1) and (2) of Council directive 79/7/EEC of 19 December 1978 on the progressive implementation of the principle of equal treatment for men and women in matters of social security must be interpreted as meaning that a child-raising allowance such as that provided by article 1 et seq. of the Bundeserziehungsgeldesetz does not fall within the scope of that directive.
